detail.title: Regression versus Classification
detail.description: For each response variable, identify whether a regression or a classification approach is more appropriate.
detail.understand: DS4A §8.3: regression predicts a quantitative response; classification predicts a categorical response. Only the TYPE OF THE RESPONSE decides — not the explanatory variables.

questions.prompt: Recognizing an image of an animal as a dog or a cat.
Predicting the age of a car.
questions.explanation: Age is a numeric quantity. (Review Q20 asks why a classification model can't predict a car's age.)

questions.prompt: Predicting wine quality on a 1-10 scale.
questions.explanation: The score is numeric and ordered, so regression is the natural fit (predictions like 6.4 can be rounded). Because it takes only 10 ordered integer values, it can also be framed as (ordinal) classification — mention both and justify the choice.

questions.prompt: Predicting whether a person is susceptible to lung cancer.
Predicting whether an SMS text is spam or not.
Predicting the energy use of appliances in a low-energy building.

common_mistakes: Deciding by the type of the inputs (an image is not 'categorical' — the label is).
Calling every number 'regression': a number used as a code (e.g. postcode) is categorical.
